threads.question:
Subject: LMIA Exemption for CSQ Holders (A75) - "employer in the Province of Quebec" Good Afternoon, I am writing to request clarification on the requirements for a work permit issued under LMIA exemption code A75 (CSQ holders in Quebec). My understanding is that eligibility rests on the applicant holding a CSQ with one of the designated codes at section 9 of their CSQ, residing in Quebec and applying to work in the province of Quebec. The IRCC page on this exemption ([https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-) citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-manuals/temporary-residents/foreign- workers/quebec-cases/labour-market-impact-assessment-exempt-work-permit-renewals-extensions-certain- quebec-selection-holders.html) states "for clarity", that the applicant must be "seeking to extend or to obtain an employer-specific work permit for an employer in the province of Quebec". It is the definition of "employer in the province of Quebec" that is the subject of this query. Does a TFW working remotely from their home in the province of Quebec for an employer that is located in another province meet the requirement for an exemption under A75? Your clarification would be appreciated. Thank you in advance for your response. Sincerely,
and Citizenship Caneda
threads.answer:

IPG ADMIN Worker Unit / Unité des travailleurs ADMIN OPI (IRCC) FW: LMIA Exemption for CSQ Holders (A75) - "employer in the Province of Quebec" --
Hello,
Does a TFW working remotely from their home in the province of Quebec for an employer that is located in
another province meet the requirement for an exemption under A75?
Yes, the employer must be located in the province of Quebec to meet the eligibility requirements under this LMIA exemption category.
With regard to remote work, the work location must be in a setting that can be inspected should the employer be selected for inspection under the employer compliance regime to ensure conditions imposed under sections 209.2 and
209.4 are met. Remote work during the pandemic is acceptable, however, the work location indicated in the offer of employ is subject to inspection to ensure the employer has provided a workplace that is free of abuse. Regards, Nancy

Good day,
Please see below the approved response.
Please find below the answer to your questions.
Q: Does this mean that the student is required to make two applications: one to extend status as a student, before their current Sp Expires, AND a simultaneous application to change conditions to a visitor, so he/she is able to remain in Canada while the new study permit is issued. A: The foreign national will need to submit both a study permit extension application to maintain their student status and an application to change conditions as a visitor as the break of studies is greater than 150 days. After changing their status, the student may resume their studies, using their previous study permit, as long as the study permit is valid.
Q: In addition, R183(S) states that Students who submit the "Application to Change Conditions, Extend My Stay or Remain in Canada As o Student" form [iMM S709] before the expiry date of the previous study permit will maintain their status as a temporary resident as per subsection R183(5), Since they maintained stotus, students are then allowed to commence studies while their SP application is in process. Kindly refer us to the regulatory authority that prevent them from beginning studies, while the study permit extension is in process pursuant to R183(5), as noted in the highlighted line above.
A: R189 states that a foreign national who has made an application under subsection 217(1) is authorized to study without a study permit until a decision is made on the application if they have remained in Canada since the expiry of their study permit and continue to comply with the conditions, other than the expiry date, set out on the expired study permit. In this situation, the student who have not resumed their studies within 150 days didn't comply with the conditions of their study permit. Therefore, R189 can not be used for students in this case.
We hope you find this information helpful.
Thank you.

Students should begin or resume their studies at their new institution within 150 days from the day that they ceased or completed their studies at the previous institution. If a student does not resume their studies within 150 days, they should do either of the following:
change their status (that is, change to visitor status or worker status)
leave Canada If they do not change their status or leave Canada, they are considered non-compliant with their study permit conditions.
After changing their status to visitor or worker, students may resume their studies, using their previous study permit, as long as the study permit is valid. If the study permit is about to expire when the student resumes their studies, the student must apply to extend their study permit in Canada, using the application to change conditions, extend your stay or remain in Canada as a student, before the expiry date.
Since students in that case have applied to extend their stay as a visitor or worker, they may not pursue their studies when their current permit expires and only resume their studies if their study permit extension is approved.
We hope that this information is helpful to you.

CMB TRES / SERV DGRC (IRCC) RE: Travel Restrictions -- REP-2022-0380 -- DUE 18-Mar-22
Under the current travel restrictions, unvaccinated foreign nationals are banned from entering Canada unless otherwise exempt by one of the exemptions listed in the entry OIC titled "Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada Order (Prohibiting of Entry into Canada)".
Pursuant to the aforementioned instrument, under 4(5)(f), the Minister of IRCC has issued a classed based entry national interest exemption for individuals who hold a passport issued by the Hong Kong Special Administration Region of People's Republic of China or by the United Kingdom to a British National (Overseas) as a person born, naturalized or registered in Hong Kong who have been approved for an open work permit, as well as family members of any nationality who have been approved for an open work permit under the temporary public policy for recent post- secondary graduates from Hong Kong.
As long as the foreign national meets the requirements of this definition and they have copies of the necessary documentation then they are eligible to enter Canada unvaccinated. That being said, the national interest exemption does not exempt them from other testing and quarantine requirements. In addition, as a foreign national who is permitted entry into Canada without qualifying as fully vaccinated, they may take a connecting flight that is scheduled to depart within 24 hours of the departure time for your flight to Canada. Foreign nationals authorized entry into Canada can continue to their final destination using their valid pre-entry molecular test as long as the scheduled departure time of their domestic flight is within 24 hours of the departure time for their flight to Canada.
Thank you,

In regards to your second question, unfortunately, a foreign national applying under the Federal Self-employed Persons Program would not be eligible for a bridging open work permit (BOWP). The BOWP is only for those who are applying for permanent residence under a program that allows them to apply for permanent residence from within Canada – which is not the case for the Self-employed permanent residence program. Apprentissage à distance depuis le Canada Si les cours que vous suiviez sont passés à un format en ligne en raison de la pandémie, le temps que vous avez passé à étudier en ligne depuis le Canada peut étre comptabilisé dans le calcul de la période de validité de votre PTPD. Est-ce simplement pour encourager les étudiants à suivre les cours en présentiel ou est-ce parce que cela pourrait compromettre l’émission de leur permis post-diplôme sans que cela ne soit clairement mentionné sur le site ?

threads.question:
and Cizenship Caneda
Hello,
I have a question in regards to the “public policy allowing certain visitors in Canada to apply for a work permit :COVID-
19 program delivery”
[https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-) manuals/service-delivery/coronavirus/temporary-residence/work-permit/visitor-work-permits.html
My main question is in regards to the eligibility requirements to apply for an employer specific work permit:
1. is in Canada with valid temporary resident status as a visitor, including status extensions under subsection 183(5) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR), that is, maintained status, at the time of work permit application submission
2. has submitted an employer-specific work permit application using the Application to Change Conditions, Extend my Stay or Remain in Canada as a Worker [IMM 5710]
3. has remained in Canada with status since application submission
4. submitted the application on or before February 28, 2023
It is the point in yellow which is confusing, does this mean that a visitor who has submitted a work permit application under this policy, but is approaching the end of their authorized visitor stay and still doesn't have a decision on their work permit, needs to now apply for a visitor record as well to ensure that they are in "status” when the work permit is assessed?
Hypothetical case scenario:
Entry as visitor Nov 1, 2021, has visitor status for six months until May 1, 2022 Applied for employer specific work permit on March 1, 2022 No answer on work permit April 30, 2022
With 1 day left in their authorized visitor stay, should we now also submit a visitor record to ensure “ they have remained in Canada with status since application (work permit) submission".
Thanks for your time and clarification,
Blank Page
Pilsworth.Laurie
threads.answer:
March 7, 2022 12:35 PM
IPG ADMIN Worker Unit / Unité des travailleurs ADMIN OPI (IRCC) FW: Inquiry-Temporary Public Policy --REP-2022-0533 -- DUE 01-APR-22
QuESTiON: It is the point in yellow which is confusing, does this mean that a visitor who has submitted a work permit application under this policy, but is approaching the end of their authorized visitor stay and still doesn't have a decision on their work permit, needs to now apply for a visitor record as well to ensure that they are in "status" when the work permit is assessed?
RESPONSE: If a temporary resident has applied to extend their status under R181 prior to its expiry, their status is extended by law under R183(5). As such a new application is not needed to extend their status until a decision is made on their application. You may find further information on this in the publically available instructions for officers here: Maintained status during processing (previously called implied status) and here R186(u)— Pending decision on work permit renewal
In your scenario:
Hypothetical case scenario:
Entry as visitor Nov 1, 2021, has visitor status for six months until May 1, 2022 Applied for employer specific work permit on March 1, 2022 No answer on work permit April 30, 2022
On March 1, 2022, if the applicant used the Application to Change Conditions, Extend my Stay or Remain in Canada as a Worker [IMM 5710] form to request and extension of their status and authority to work, then they have met the requirement of R181 in that they applied for an extension prior to the expiration of their status, so on May 1, 2022 they would continue to maintain their status by law under R183(5) until a decision is made on the work permit application submitted March 1, 2022.

Students who are already in Canada and have applied for a co-op work permit may begin their co-op placement using their on-campus and off-campus work authorization, provided they meet all the eligibility requirements.

Please see below the responses to your enquiries.
An applicant does not need to be a Doctor in “Philosophy” to apply under this category, correct? For example, an applicant has a doctor degree in Life science. Yes, Ph.D. stands for Doctor in Philosophy, which is a doctorate in any discipline.
It is not absolutely necessary that the applicant has an award as the IRCC guide says “Post-doctoral fellows can either be the direct recipients of an award OR be offered a time-limited position to undertake research on behalf of or as part of a team of researchers", is it correct? Correct, the applicant must have completed, or be expecting to complete shortly, their doctorate and be working in a field related to that in which they earned, or are earning, their Ph.D. Post-doctoral fellows can either be the direct recipients of an award or be offered a time-limited position to undertake research on behalf of or as part of a team of researchers

threads.subject: Ask for advice on two issues -- REP-2022-0222 -- DUE 2-Mar-22
threads.question:
Dear officer,
I amManager of and an RCIC in good standing. I would like to ask for your advice and guidance on two issues.
1) Timeline for applying for study permit extension and a new TRV from within Canada. The current processing time for study permit extension is 60 days (2 months) while for TRV applications submitted from within Canada the processing time is 156 days (5 months). A student needs 7 months or longer to get their study permit extended and have a new TRV before they can travel.
We usually advise students to apply for study permit extension 3-4 months before their study permit expires under normal circumstance (e. g. before COVID) and normally, it usually takes a month or so for study permit extension and another month or two for a new TRV. Due to the current long processing time, is it safe to say students can apply for study permit extension 7-8 months ahead of time or apply for study permit extension as early as they want? In the past before COVID, students were often refused for their study permit extension applications or their applications were returned due to the reason that they applied too early.
2) Study permit requirement for short term students to travel to Canada. As you know, IRCC recently updated PDI on study permit. Applicants may apply for a PGWP from within Canada if their study permit is still valid or they meet one of the other requirements of section R199.
Applicants whose study permit becomes invalid or expires before they apply for a PGWP are not eligible to work without a permit under paragraph R186(w) and must either
leave Canada and apply for a PGWP from overseas or apply to restore their status as a student by applying for a PGWP with the correct fees ($255) and paying the fees to restore their status as a student ($350)
As per paragraph R186(w), graduates who apply for a work permit, such as a post-graduation work permit, before the expiry of their study permit are eligible to work full time without a work permit while waiting for a decision on their application if all of the following apply:
They are or were the holders of a valid study permit at the time of the post-graduation work permit application. They have completed their program of study. They met the requirements for working off campus without a work permit under paragraph R186(v) (that is, they were a full-time student enrolled at a DLl in a post-secondary academic, vocational or professional training program of at least 8 months in duration that led to a degree, diploma or certificate). They did not exceed the allowable hours of work under paragraph R186(v).
Applicants remain eligible to work full time without a work permit while waiting for a decision on their application even after leaving and re-entering Canada.

threads.answer:
IPG Student Unit Admin / Admin Unité des étudiants OPI (IRCC)
### IPG Student Unit Admin / Admin Unité des étudiants OPI (IRCC)
Good day,
Please see below the approved response.
Please find below the answer to your questions.
1. Is the spouse of an international student who has this condition allowed to apply to change conditions on their current work permit with an explanation that they would like to continue working why their spouse is graduating and applying for a PGWP? Response: yes. Normally, their work permit is valid for the same amount of time that their spouse or common-law partner's work permit or study permit is valid. Their work permit will stay valid for that entire period even if
- their spouse or common-law partner's situation changes, for example 0they lose their job they complete their studies early
- they divorce or separate
If these situations apply to them, they won't be able to extend their work permit when it expires, but they may be eligible for another type of work permit. More information may be found here.
2. Is the spouse allowed to work when their spouse is enrolled part-time in their last semester? For immigration purposes a students who has been enrolled full time throughout their studies, is considered as full time students if enrolled part time solely in their last semester. Response: No, they must comply with their work permit conditions which doesn't allow them to work when their spouse is not enrolled full time.
3. The study permit is valid for 90 days after completion of the program of study, if a spouse has this condition on their work permit, would they be allowed to work during the 90 days period after completion? Or they have to stop working when the last term ends? Response: No, they are not allowed to work until the principal applicant's work permit has been approved.

threads.answer:
IPG Student Unit Admin / Admin Unité des étudiants OPI (IRCC)
IPG Student Unit Admin / Admin Unité des étudiants OPI (IRCC)
APR-22
Good day,
Please see below the approved response.
Students who have completed a program of study and will be starting a new program of study within 150 days of receiving a written confirmation of program completion from their current institution may work off campus on a full-time basis until the start of their new program if the following applies:
they meet the eligibility criteria to work off campus [R186(v)] they have received written confirmation of program completion from their current institution (for instance, a
transcript or an official letter)
they have submitted an application to change conditions, extend their stay or remain in Canada as a student before their current study permit expired, or they still have a valid study permit they have been issued a letter of acceptance to a subsequent program of full-time study at a DLl and will be starting the new program within 150 calendar days of receiving a notification of program completion from their current institution
If the new program of study starts more than 150 calendar days after the first date they receive written confirmation of program completion from their current institution, they should then either apply to change their status (change it into visitor status or worker) or leave Canada until their new program commences.
Students who have applied to extend their stay in Canada as a student are required to cease working if their study permit application is refused.
For further details: [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/work-off-campus.html#new](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/work-off-campus.html#new)

** Super visa applications must be submitted outside of Canada, which means that the clients should be physically outside of Canada at the time of the application. If a client is currently in Canada, they are ineligible to apply. Even if the on-line application portal(s) allows clients to submit super visa applications while residing in Canada, the applications would be cancelled by the processing office. Temporary resident visas (TRVs), including super visas, cannot be extended. If a client wishes to apply for a new TRV they must apply outside of Canada. Votre certificat demeure valide pour lobtention de votre permis d’études dans le cas ou votre admission serait reportée de la session d’automne à la session de l'hiver qui suit. Lorsque vous aurez obtenu votre permis d’études. votre certificat demeurera valide même si vous changez d’établissement d’enseignement ou de programme d’études. pourvu qu'l s'agisse d'un programme de méme durée, de méme niveau ou de même cycle. Pour tout autre cnangement, vous devrez obtenir un nouveau certificat
Est-ce que nous devons en conclure que si un élève a obtenu son permis d’études (ou sa confirmation de permis d’études), il peut utiliser le même CAQ même si il change de cohorte (pour la même formation)? Par contre, s’il n’a pas encore obtenu son permis d’études, il devrait demander un nouveau CAQ en cas de report autre que pour la session d’automne vers la session d’hiver... Nous avions eu l’information que les CAQ étaient valident de la session d’automne (août à décembre) vers la session d’hiver (janvier à avril), mais que pour tout autre changement, l’étudiant devait demander un nouveau CAQ (peu importe s’il a obtenu son permis d’études ou non).
Voici ma question pour les demandeurs d’asile qui souhaitent étudier au Québec : Un demandeur d’asile n’a pas de statut légal au Canada en attendant la décision, mais peut avoir un permis de travail ou un permis d’études sur lequel il est indiqué que le document n’octroie pas un statut temporaire. La plupart des demandeurs d’asile n’ont aucun statut légal au Canada, mais sont autorisés à demeurer sur le territoire dans l’attente de la décision relative à leur demande. À ce titre, ils doivent détenir un document qui les autorise à étudier, quelle que soit la durée de leur programme. L’exemption de l’obligation de détenir un permis d’études pour des études d’une durée de moins de six mois ne s’applique donc pas aux demandeurs d’asile majeurs. Cependant, l’exemption reste valide pour la personne qui dispose d’un statut de résident temporaire au pays et qui demande l’asile au Canada pendant la période de séjour autorisée, dans la mesure où elle termine ce cours ou ce programme avant la fin de la période de séjour autorisée. Les étrangers qui sont autorisés à entrer au Canada détiennent un statut à titre de résidents temporaires. Tous les demandeurs qui sont admissibles pour un visa doivent le détenir pour entrer au Canada. La plupart des demandeurs d’asile sont admis au Canada sans avoir obtenu au préalable un visa de résident temporaire et ainsi ils sont inadmissibles sous A41(1) de la Loi sur les l’immigration et la protection des réfugiés et sous R6 du Règlement sur l’immigration et la protection des réfugiés pour ne pas avoir un visa lors de leur entrée au Canada.

R/La plupart des demandeurs d'asile n'ont aucun statut légal au Canada, mais sont autorisés à rester au pays dans l'attente d'une décision au sujet de leur demande. Ils sont habituellement assujettis à une mesure de renvoi non exécutoire. Ils ne peuvent bénéficier d’une dispense de l'obligation d'obtenir un permis d'études accordée pour des études ou un programme d'études de courte durée [R188(1)c)] puisque le cours ou le programme d'études doit, dans un tel cas, être achevé avant la fin de la période du séjour autorisé – lequel séjour autorisé est inexistant dans leur cas.

threads.answer:
Hello,
Thank you for your question. Please see our response below.
QUESTION I have a quick question regarding work experience. I understand work is considered the services for which salary is paid or commission is earned but if someone works in lieu of boarding and lodging, would that be considered as work? In other words, if someone was not paid any salary but was allowed to stay in a house for which the person did not pay any rent but performed household chores, would this be considered as work?
ANSWER: Information on what is considered as "work" is available on our webpage Temporary Foreign Worker and International Mobility Programs: What is work? Work is defined in the Regulations as an activity for which wages are paid or commission is earned, or that competes directly with the activities of Canadian citizens or permanent residents in the Canadian labour market, i.e., Can a Canadian citizen or permanent resident do this work? Please review the section on what is not considered to be “work".
In addition, another factor to consider is the type of relationship between the individual who performs household chores and the main occupant/primary resident of the home. Is there an employer/employee relationship? Also, is this a short- or long-term arrangement? Would this experience have an impact on the future employment of the individual performing household chores?
We hope you will find this information useful and thank you for your patience.

RESPONSE: Yes, you understand correctly. Jenny's new work permit would not be issued under the LMIA- exempt administrative codes C41 or C42. The reason the biometrics are not valid for ten years is because a partial biometric enrolment (fingerprints only) was collected at a Service Canada location and since it was a partial enrolment, it does not qualify for the 1 in 10 validity. 40(2)(a) states: the permanent resident or the foreign national continues to be inadmissible for misrepresentation for a period of 5- years following, in the case of a determination OUTSIDE Canada, a final determination of inadmissibility under subsection (1) or,
In the case of a determination IN Canada, the date the removal order is enforced.
More specifically,
For those found inadmissible for misrepresentation in Canada, the period of inadmissibility begins on the
date the removal order is enforced. If the removal order is enforced on November 21, 2014, or later, the period of inadmissibility is five years, as is the ban on applications for permanent residence. If the removal order is enforced on November 20, 2014, or before, then the period of inadmissibility is two years and there is no ban on applications for permanent residence. For those found inadmissible outside of Canada, the period of inadmissibility begins on the date of the refusal letter. If the refusal letter is dated November 21, 2014, or later, the period of inadmissibility is five years as is the ban on applications for permanent residence. If the refusal letter is dated November 20, 2014, or sooner, the period of inadmissibility is two years and there is no ban on applications for permanent residence.

When a temporary resident submits an application to restore their status as a worker or student, the client is submitting two applications in one; the first is to restore their status as a temporary resident, while the second is to seek authorization as a worker or student. An applicant can only restore their status to that of a temporary resident and to the authorization that they held immediately prior to the restoration application.
A temporary resident who held a work permit and lost their status can apply in Canada for restoration of their temporary resident status and authorization to work within 90 days of having lost their status. In addition to applying for restoration and a new work permit, they may also apply for a study permit, and pay the fees, if they meet the requirements for study permit issuance. The study permit will only be assessed after the work permit and restoration applications are approved.
Please note that since a restoration application is submitted with the purpose of restoring the applicant's status as a temporary resident, they are limited to seek their authorization (i.e. as a worker or student) to what they previously held. That said, an out-of-status worker or student may apply to restore their status as a visitor without submitting an application (and the associated fees) for a work or study permit. However, restoring their status as a visitor may limit them to later apply for a work or study permit from inside Canada (only if eligible).
You may find more information on our website.

RE: ICT-Specialized Knowledge to Manager Category and Maximum Duration
Please note that this service provides guidance, therefore, we cannot provide case-specific advice.
The purpose of the Intra-Company Transferee provisions is to transfer knowledge or expertise to Canada.
The eligibility requirements for ICT require that: "the foreign national be employed (via payroll or contract) continuously (full-time, not accumulated part-time) by the enterprise outside Canada, in a similar full-time position, for at least one year within the three- year period immediately preceding the date of initial application".
In cases where the foreign national entered Canada under the ICT provisions for the transfer of Specialized Knowledge to the Canadian operation, they would not meet the requirements for an ICT executive or senior managerial position as the experience in a similar position needs to be acquired outside Canada within the previous 3 years, thus an applicant who being promoted to a senior manager would have to acquire experience as a senior manager or similar position outside Canada in order to meet the eligibility as an executive or senior manager. As you may be aware, the maximum period allowed under the ICT provisions is 5 years for Specialized Knowledge and 7 years for executives and senior manager. In addition, ICT applicants must demonstrate that they are coming to Canada for a temporary period only and that they will comply with all immigration requirements for temporary entry.
We would also like to highlight that the assessment of an application is based on a case-by-case basis, considering the particular circumstances in conjunction with the supporting documentation available to the officer. The onus is always on the applicant to provide sufficient documentation to satisfy an officer that they meet the requirements.
For additional information about intra-company transferees, please visit the Canada.ca website.

threads.question:
Hello,
I hope this message finds you well. I am writing with a policy question on behalf of our team here at the University of
Victoria, related to students' eligibility to work off campus in between two programs of study.
We understand that students who have completed a program of study and will be starting a new program of study may work for up to 150 days in between programs, provided they hold a valid study permit, have received written confirmation of program completion the first program and a letter of acceptance from the subsequent program, and provided they meet the eligibility criteria to work off campus (R186(v)).
Citoyenneté Canada
With regard to the requirement to meet the eligibility criteria under R186(v), can you please clarify if a student who is enrolled full time in the final term of their first program of study and will be enrolled full time in their subsequent program, would be eligible to work in between programs even if they studied part time in a previous term? For example:
- An international student enrolled in Program A studies part time for one term (September-December 2020, not their final term). They are full time in all other academic terms of the program. The student then studies full-time in their final term of Program A (January-April 2022) and is eligible to work off-campus for up to 20 hours per week during that term. Upon completion of the Program A in April 2022, the student receives official written confirmation of program completion from the DLI. The student receives a letter of acceptance for Program B, which will begin in September 2022 (less than 150 days after completing Program A). threads.answer:
HK residents
Hello,
Thank you for contacting the Immigration Representatives mailbox. We hope the following answers your questions.
1. Can a visitor in Canada submit a (outside Canada) online TRV application? OR does the applicant need to be physically outside Canada in order to apply? As I understand, it does not require the applicant to be physically outside Canada in order to submit a TRV application, since it is an online application. We will just need to use the outside Canada application package. Only foreign nationals who hold a valid work or study permit and are in Canada are eligible to apply for a temporary resident visa from within Canada and only under certain conditions. All other foreign nationals must apply outside Canada. If your client is currently in Canada, they are ineligible to apply for a TRV. Even if the on-line application portal(s) allows clients to submit TRV applications while residing in Canada, the applications would be cancelled by the processing office. Under the current Mls, all applications for a temporary resident visa (including a transit visa), a work permit or a study permit submitted by foreign nationals who are outside Canada at the time of the application must be submitted using electronic means (meaning applicants must apply online).
2. If a super visa applicant arrives in Canada with a valid regular visitor visa, and then the super visa application is approved while he/she is in Canada, can this applicant submit the passport for visa stamp in Ottawa and then go to the border to activate his/her two years' stay? Super visas are issued and printed outside of Canada only. In the scenario you describe, the applicant would have to leave Canada to get their super visa counterfoil affixed to their passport and then return to Canada to benefit from a stay of up to two years. Q3. As per the temporary public policy creating two pathways to permanent residence to facilitate the immigration of certain Hong Kong residents, one of the eligibility requirements for permanent residence is to be physically present in Canada at the time when an application for permanent residence under this public policy is made, and at the time of granting of permanent residence. While short absences from Canada are allowed (e.g. vacation, business trips, visit a family member), if the applicant is not in Canada at time of PR finalization, the processing office will inform the applicant that they must provide evidence that they are returning to Canada. Failure to do so may result in a refusal for not meeting the eligibility requirements of the public policy. ********************************** Regards,
Citoyenneté Canada

Only foreign nationals who hold a valid work or study permit and are in Canada are eligible to apply for a temporary resident visa from within Canada and only under certain conditions. threads.subject: Permanent Residency under the Hong Kong Pathway Stream B
threads.question:
Dear Sir/Madam,
I am a legal representative and I have an enquiry concerning the Stream B permanent residence pathway for Hong Kong resident.
My enquiry is concerning the definition of full-time employment. According to IRCC regulations, full-time employment consists at least 30 hours of work over a period of one week.
and Citizenshi Canada et Ciloyeneé Canada
However, the definition is unclear if the client has a flexible working hours. For example, the client may work 20hours one week, but 40 hours another, etc. Assuming he accumulates more than 1560 hours in a year or have an average of 30 hours or higher per week, will he be eligible to apply for permanent residency via PR as having worked full-time for a year?
Alternatively, if he is considered part-time, then may he apply for PR after one year once he obtains 1560 hours or he must wait for three years before applying?
Best regards,
and Cizenship Canedaot Citoyenneté Canada
threads.answer:
Dear
Thank you for contacting the Immigration Representative Mailbox. You will find the answer to your question below.
Applicants in Stream B must have accumulated 1 year (12 months) of full-time (at least 30 hours per week, or the equivalent in part-time, for a total of at least 1,560 hours) authorized Canadian work experience at any skill level within
the 3 years before they apply.
For part-time work, applicants can work more or less than 15 hours/week as long as it adds up to 1,560 hours within the 3 years before they apply.
For full-time work, we do not count any hours of work above 30 hours/week. A reasonable period of vacation time will be counted towards meeting the work experience requirement.
In the example you provided where an applicant sometimes works 20 hours per week and sometimes 40 hours per week, a maximum of 30 hours would be calculated for the weeks where the applicant worked 40 hours. If the applicant worked for less than 30 hours for some weeks of the year, than the applicant will not have accumulated 1,560 hours in one year and will need more than a year to meet a total of 1,560 hours of work experience.
We trust this information will assist you.
Sincerely,
The Immigration Representative Mailbox

threads.question:

My question is whether accompanying dependent children who are present in Canada can be included in two separate PR applications of their divorced parents which are being processed concurrently: the parents were divorced a long time ago, the mother has an H&C in process for over a year, whereas the father recently submitted a PR application in the family class (sponsorship by CML spouse).
Details:

Since that time, the PA's ex-husband entered Canada and began living common-law with a Canadian spouse.
PA's ex-husband and his new spouse recently submitted an inland sponsorship application (not my clients), including the same two daughters as dependents in that later application.
Can the dependents remain in the mother's H&C application and receive PR via whichever application is approved first, or must they be removed from the mother's H&C in order to receive PR via the father's sponsorship application?

mother's H&C application until such time as the father's application is approved.

threads.answer:
Dear
If a person has been included in a humanitarian and compassionate (H&C) application as a dependent, they are considered to have a pending H&C application. Therefore, a second application for H&C consideration should not be examined and there are no exceptions.
While the applications can be processed concurrently, the father will be unable to request H&C consideration for his daughters within their family class application while the H&C application initiated by their mother continues to be processed.
Sincerely,

Hello,
Thank you for contacting the Immigration Representatives mailbox. We hope the following answers your question. ***
Please find below the answers to your questions.
1. Post August 31, 2022 -- Will students be able to begin their study outside Canada in an online delivery mode of a program that has on-campus and online delivery options-without jeopardizing their ability to receive a study visa/permit to transition into the on-campus version of the same program in Canada? Response: Under normal circumstances, Since by definition distance learning does not require one to be in Canada, a study permit cannot be issued for this type of course. However, some distance learning courses include an in-Canada portion to the program (e.g., special tutorials or the writing of final exams). If the overall course of study is greater than six months, then the student requires a study permit for the in-Canada portion of the program, even if the in-Canada portion is less than six months. The duration of the study permit should be for the duration of the in-Canada portion only. You may find more information on our website
2. Once the temporary policy is rescinded, will it be expected that a student cannot commence an on-campus program in an online manner without a Study Permit approval? Response: Foreign nationals are required to obtain a study permit for engaging in academic, professional, vocational or other education or training that is more than 6 months in duration at a designated learning institution (DLl) in Canada. The following activities are not considered studies for the purposes of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA) and do not require a study permit: pre-school (pre-kindergarten) courses of general interest or self-improvement distance learning audited courses (typically by sitting in on an academic course, but without obtaining credit for it, or having the ability to obtain credit for it retroactively)
More information can be found here
3. Will there be unintended consequences for post-secondary institutions (i.e. jeopardizing the DLl status) and/or the students (i.e. ineligibility for a Study Permit) if the institutions continue to run programs where students can start abroad and then apply for a Study Permit to come to Canada and complete the program? Response: some distance learning courses include an in-Canada portion to the program (e.g., special tutorials or the writing of final exams). If the overall course of study is greater than six months, then the student requires a study permit

for the in-Canada portion of the program, even if the in-Canada portion is less than six months. The duration of the study permit should be for the duration of the in-Canada portion only.
4. Will courses completed by international students in Canada on a study permit but online be counted as online or on-campus courses? (Noting the 50+% on-campus requirement for PGWP)? Response: If their courses were moved online due to the pandemic, the time they spend studying online from within Canada still counts toward the length of their PGWP. However, it's highly recommended that they attend in-class options when offered. We don't have a specific end date yet for the temporary policy changes for in-Canada students studying online. More information can be found here.
5. If a student has commenced a program and is studying outside of Canada for a significant duration of their program during the COVID-19 August 31, 2022 allowance, does that impact their potential to get a study permit? i.e. The distance education rule re: study permits. What about after the COVID-19 allowances end? Response: To be eligible for the temporary policy changes to the Post-Graduation Work Permit Program (PGWPP), students (enrolled in PGWP-eligible programs in progress in March 2020 or who began or will begin PGWP-eligible programs between spring 2020 and summer 2022) must meet one of the following requirements:
- have a study permit
- have been approved for a study permit have submitted a study permit application prior to beginning their program and have eventually been approved.
Please note that all foreign nationals who meet all requirements to apply for a study permit are eligible for a study permit at any time.
6. A student completes a credential (degree, diploma, etc.) from another institution outside Canada. Courses completed to earn that credential are then used to obtain transfer credits for a program at a Designated Learning Institution. How do transfer credits impact an application for a Post Graduation Work Permit?
7. Specifically, how will the transfer credits impact:
1. The students' eligibility for/length of PGWP;
2. The number of courses the student must complete on campus (50+% rule);
3. The length of the student's study permit.
Response for questions 6 and 7: A student attends a foreign post-secondary institution and transfers to an accredited provincial or territorial post-secondary institution in Canada to complete their studies. In this scenario, if the qualifying educational credential were issued from an institution outside Canada, the student would not qualify for a post-graduation work permit. However, if the student received their educational credential from an eligible Canadian DLl, only the time they studied in Canada would factor into their eligibility for a post-graduation work permit. More information can be found here. Once an officer has determined that an applicant is bona fide and meets the requirements, they are to issue a long-term study permit, along with a long-term multiple-entry TRV or an eTA, if applicable, for the length of studies plus 90 days or passport expiry, whichever comes first. More information can be found here.
8. Does this hold true if the student started in an online (non-PGWP eligible) program and then transfers credits into an on-campus PGWP-eligible program? Response: A student attends their first year at a private post-secondary institution in Canada that is not eligible for the PGWPP but then transfers to an eligible DLI. In this scenario, if the student completed their program of study at the eligible DLl, they may be eligible for a post-graduation work permit but only for the length of time they studied at the eligible DLI. We hope that this information is helpful to you. ***

worker -- REP-2022-0332
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox. We appreciate your patience.
Question: The representatives and applicants are in a tight spot when an employer refuses to give an employment letter to a federal skilled worker for their immigration application. In such situation, they get a court affidavit of support paper from their senior for proof of their work experience for that organization.
I want to know what is IRCC policy for proof of work experience in absence of employment letter on company letterhead? Is a court affidavit substitutable document in this scene for proof of work experience for an express entry or Canadian experience class skilled worker, along with pay slips, form 16/T4slips and ITRs?
Answer: Principal applicants are requested to provide documentary evidence of their work experience in Canada through a combination of: a copy of their most recent work permit (unless they are work-permit exempt), copies of their most recent T4 tax information slips and Notice of Assessment (NOA) issued by the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) or a
sufficient combination of other supporting documentation, and employer letters of reference for all periods of
qualifying work experience claimed in the application.
Canadian employers are responsible for deducting and remitting Canada Pension Plan (CPP) contributions, Employment Insurance (EI) premiums, and income tax from remuneration or other amounts they pay to their employees to the CRA. They must also provide employees with a record of their remuneration and deductions in the form of a T4 tax information slip. The T4 slip is therefore key documentary evidence for the vast majority of CEC applicants to demonstrate that they were in an employer-employee work relationship during their period of qualifying work experience in Canada.
However, there is no obligation under the regulations that CEC applicants provide a T4 tax information slip or NOA specifically with their application, and these particular documents cannot be considered conclusive evidence or the only evidence accepted for the purposes of substantiating whether an applicant has qualifying Canadian work experience. As such, in the absence of a T4 tax information slip or NOA, documents which may help substantiate the applicant's work experience in Canada could include a record or letter of employment from the Canadian employer, work contracts and pay stubs.
In all cases, the onus is on the applicant to establish that they meet the CEC criteria at the time of their application. All applicants are required to provide satisfactory evidence of their work experience in Canada, including the fact that they were in an employer-employee relationship during their period of qualifying work experience.
Applicants should also include any documentation from their employer stating that they will not provide an employment letter.
We trust that this information will assist you.

Sincerely,

Pour les étudiants à l’intérieur du Canada, une lettre d’approbation n’est pas suffisante pour permettre l’inscription d’un étudiant étranger, à moins qu’une autorisation d’étudier y soit clairement indiquée. Les informations indiquées sur la lettre d’approbation prennent autorité.

threads.question:
Good day! We know that if WES has evaluated a degree as Dual Bachelor's, client is awarded bachelor's degree CRS points. What if Client studied two programs (joint degree) at the same time in four years at a Canadian university and was awarded two separate bachelor degree diplomas? In that case, do they get the Two Diplomas CRS points?
Thank you for your time.
and Cizenship Canedaot Citoyenneté Canada
threads.answer:
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox.
Question:
Good day! We know that if WES has evaluated a degree as Dual Bachelor's, client is awarded bachelor's degree CRS points. What if Client studied two programs (joint degree) at the same time in four years at a Canadian university and was awarded two separate bachelor degree diplomas? In that case, do they get the Two Diplomas CRS points?
Answer:
If the foreign educational institute website and/or the diplomas themselves distinguish between how long each of those bachelor's degrees took and at least one of them was 3+ years long, then the client would get CRS points for two or more post-secondary program credentials, at least one of which must have been issued on completion of a post-secondary program of three years or longer. However, if no time distinction is made between the two degrees on the website or on the diplomas (e.g., the website just says "complete both degrees in 4 years") or there is a distinction but the time for each diploma is less than 3 years, then would not get the two diplomas CRS points.
We trust that this information will assist you.
Sincerely,

Background
Section 108 of the Règlement sur l’immigration au Québec (RIQ), which came into
effect on August 2, 2018, specifies that CSQs issued after the coming into force of the section are valid for a duration of 24 months or until IRCC renders a decision on the permanent residence application.
Since August 2, 2018, MIFI no longer renews CSQs, as they are issued for 24 months
and are valid for the duration of the permanent residence application, even if the 24-
month period has passed. In addition, CSQs issued before August 2, 2018, are valid for
the duration of the permanent residence application, even if the initial 36 months have
passed.

Eligibility requirements
To be eligible for a work permit issued under paragraph R205(a) and exemption code A75 as the holder of a CSQ, a foreign national must
- currently reside in Quebec

It is both, the employment and the employers must be located in Quebec. We will update the program delivery instructions to include this clarification. Also
While temporary foreign workers (TFWs) were allowed to work from their home in Canada on a temporary basis due to the pandemic, this is no longer in place. As you are aware, the location of work is part of the conditions imposed on the employee under section 185 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR). Question: In this case the dependent applicant's status has expired after 90 days. Is still the dependent eligible to apply for the restoration?
Response: Section 182 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR) specifies that an officer can only restore status within 90 days of the loss of status for specific reasons. To obtain temporary resident status after its loss and more then 90 days have passed, the foreign national must leave Canada and then seek entry as a temporary resident. The border service officer will have to be satisfied that the foreign national will comply with all conditions of entry including length of stay. The other option is to submit an application for extension of status in Canada and request

threads.answer:
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox. We appreciate your patience.
Question:
My client obtained 3 years of PGWP valid until December 11, 2023. When he applied for the PGWP he only needed to show the proof of his commercial pilot's licence and not the certificate of conclusion from the school. After working one year as a flight instructor, he would like to apply for the permanent residence.
a) Since these training programs does not issue a certificate/diploma and transcripts, how can the Immigration office assess his education equivalence? He only has flight hours notes, receipts of payment and enrollment letter from these schools that he attended.
b) Is there any specific permanent residence path for Pilots or Flight Instructors? Answer:
a) The applicant would not receive any CRS points for the training they completed from the flight school. While the flight school maybe recognized by IRCC as a Designated Learning Institution (DLl), it is not a recognized public or private institution that has been given authority to grant degrees, diplomas, or other credentials by a public or private act of the provincial/territorial legislature or through a government-mandated quality assurance mechanism. You may check the Canadian Information Centre for International Credentials directory to see if an institution is recognized. Please note that CRS points will only be awarded for Canadian educational credentials that are granted by educational institutions that have the legal status of “recognized” or certain specific degrees, diplomas, or other credentials that an institution was “authorized” to grant. These institutions will have the legal status of “authorized." In order to receive CRS points for education the applicant must meet the requirements as outlined in the Ministerial Instructions (Ml) 11(3) and MI 30(1)-(5). [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/mandate/policies-operational-instructions-agreements/ministerial-instructions/express-entry-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/mandate/policies-operational-instructions-agreements/ministerial-instructions/express-entry-) application-management-system/current.html

threads.subject: Extension of PGWP due to passport expiry
threads.question:
Dear Immreps:
I am a lawyer in Ontario -
I have two urgent PGWP related questions. They both relate to an application for extension of a PGWP due to passport expiry (not the 2022-04-22 PGWP extension announcement due to the pandemic). Thank you in advance for your assistance.
1. To be eligible for the regular PGWP extension due one's passport expiring before the PGWP's validity period ended (i.e. was owed a 3 year PGWP but only got a 1 year PGWP bc passport was expiring), does one have to apply for the extension before the initial PGWP expires? IRCĆ guidance simply says one must "apply for a work permit extension upon the renewal of their passport to receive the full validity of their PGWP (emphasis added)." IRCC guidance does not say that one must apply for the PGWP extension before the initial PGWP expires. I'm not worried about creating maintained status/maintaining the ability to work during processing of the extension. If the answer is yes, can you please tell me on what authority?
2. Similarly, how long can one delay applying for the PGWP extension based on passport expiry? Again, all I can find is that one should just apply "upon the renewal of their passport." How soon after renewal of the passport must one apply? If the applicant has a new passport but wants to delay submission of the PGWP extension application until after he enrolls in and graduates from a new study program in Canada in a different field, so he can use the remainder of time on the PGWP to gain work experience in his new field, is that permissible?
Thank you!
threads.answer:
Good day,
Please see below responses to your inquiries.
1. To be eligible for the regular PGWP extension due one's passport expiring before the PGWP's validity period ended (i.e. was owed a 3 year PGWP but only got a 1 year PGWP bc passport was expiring), does one have to apply for the extension before the initial PGWP expires? IRCC guidance simply says one must "apply for a work permit extension upon the renewal of their passport to receive the full validity of their PGWP (emphasis added)." IRCC guidance does not say that one must apply for the PGWP extension before the initial PGWP expires. I'm not worried about creating maintained status/maintaining the ability to work during processing of the extension. If the answer is yes, can you please tell me on what authority?
If clients' passport expires before the full predetermined length of their PGWP, then in order to extend the duration of their PGWP to reach the full length, they will need to extend their work permit by applying for a new work permit with their new passport. Please note clients must apply on paper if they're extending their PGWP and that they can only extend their PGWP if their passport expired before their PGWP's validity period. For more information please visit our website.
2. Similarly, how long can one delay applying for the PGWP extension based on passport expiry? Again, all I can find is that one should just apply "upon the renewal of their passport." How soon after renewal of the passport must one apply? If the applicant has a new passport but wants to delay submission of the PGWP extension application until after he enrolls in and graduates from a new study program in Canada in a different field, so he can use the remainder of time on the PGWP to gain work experience in his new field, is that permissible?
Clients should apply for the remaining length of their PGWP when they obtain their new passport to ensure they received their permit in a timely manner. While waiting for a decision on their PGWP extension, clients can work full-time as long they continue to meet all requirements for PGWP.
I hope that this information is helpful to you. *****************
Thank you,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.subject: Question regarding restructuring of organization
threads.question:
Dear Sir/Madam,
I am writing on behalf of my client in order to obtain some guidance from IRCC on the implications of potential corporate restructuring and the impact it will have on the temporary foreign workers (who are on LMIA based Work Permits) that will form part of the re-organization. Please note that we reached out to ESDC to obtain an opinion on this matter but they advised that they could not provide a written opinion and that we would need to reach out to IRCC for guidance. As such, we are reaching out to you for guidance and input.
Scenario 1:
Our Client is undertaking a corporate reorganization to better align the legal entity structure with its business. The reorganization is occurring within a related corporate group and is intended to be effected on a tax deferred basis. However, there are several technical rules which require careful consideration to achieve the intended result which are creating uncertainty as to whether a successor in interest can be established.
Currently, multiple businesses are comingled in the same legal entity (“OldCo”). Further, certain tangible assets integral to the operation of the businesses of OldCo are maintained in separate legal entities (“LeaseCos”). The existing structure, which has evolved through a series of recent acquisitions, amalgamations, and financing activities, is leading to commercial, financial and tax inefficiencies. The contemplated reorganization would involve the transfer of one or more of the businesses of OldCo (“Transferred Business”) to separate, newly formed corporations ("NewCo's”) on a tax deferred basis.
NewCo would acquire all (or substantially all) of the property that is reasonably necessary for NewCo to carry on the Transferred Business, including the employment of any temporary foreign workers engaged in the Transferred Business. However, it may not be possible for NewCo to assume all of the obligations and liabilities of the Transferred Business due to limitations inherent in effecting the transaction on a tax deferred basis. Further, due to the existence of multiple businesses in OldCo, all of the assets and liabilities of OldCo will not be assumed by any one single NewCo after the corporate restructuring.
We believe that based on the scenario above, the NewCo would be a successor in interest as it has substantially assumed the interests and obligations, assets and liabilities of the original owner and it continues to operate the same type of business as the original owner.
We also note that all terms and conditions of the foreign workers' employment (i.e. wages, duties, employment location) will remain the same after the transfer of the workers to NewCo. The client would also be sure to inform ESDC/SC in writing of the change in employers.
In light of this, we believe the NewCo is not obligated to obtain a new LMiA and the temporary worker is not obligated to obtain a new work permit and should continue to be authorized to work in Canada for the duration of the period stated on the existing work permit.
Question 1: Given the scenario above, would the NewCo be considered a successor in interest from IRCC's perspective such that the temporary foreign workers that are transferred to the NewCo will not need a new LMIA or a new work permit?
Scenario 2:
Alternatively, the Client is considering a smaller scale reorganization with a more limited purpose of partially addressing the financial inefficiencies in the existing structure. A separate legal entity would be formed within the organization (“ServiceCo”) to employ and manage a section or a large part of the workforce, including temporary foreign workers. The intent is to have a centralized administration and management function within the group to produce operational efficiencies and other cost savings. The ServiceCo structure will also enable consistent provision of compensation and benefits to employees across the organization and help to better manage financial and compliance risks as compared to the existing structure. The ServiceCo may be further aligned by region or function.
We also note that all terms and conditions of the foreign worker's employment (i.e. wages, duties, employment location) will remain the same after the transfer of the workers to ServiceCo. The client would also be sure to inform
ESDC/SC in writing of the change in employers.
Question 2: Given the scenario above, would ServiceCo be considered a successor in interest from IRCC's perspective such that the temporary foreign workers that are transferred to the NewCo will not need a new LMIA or a new work permit?
Thank you for your assistance with this matter. I look forward to hearing back from you.

threads.answer:
Good afternoon,
Thank you for reaching out to the IPG mailbox. Please see the answer to your question below.
Question: If the main applicant has completed her studies and has an accompanying spouse, who was on an open work permit.(C-42)
Now when the main applicant applied for a post-graduate work permit, she or he is under implied status; Can she apply for the spousal open work permit extension, if she is working or going to work in a skilled occupation? Can the PGWP application and spousal open work permit be applied at the same time? What is the status of the spouse going to be currently? who was on an OWP before?
Response: When the study permit holder applies for a post-graduate work permit, if they apply before their study permit expires, they will have the authority to work without a permit under R186(w) and maintained status under R183(5) until the work permit is approved and issued.
The dependent spouse who presently holds an open work permit issued as the spouse of a study permit holder, may apply for a new open work permit if the principal worker is presently employed and will remain employed in a NOC 0, A or B occupation. Should an application for a new type of work permit be made before the expiry of the existing C-42 permit, then the applicant would be able to continue working without a work permit under R186(u) as long as they do not leave the country and abide by the same conditions on their existing permit. If the spouse does not apply for another work permit before the expiry of the existing permit then the spouse will lose authorization to work in Canada and need to apply for a new authorization, change their status, or leave the country.
Yes, the PGWP application and the spousal Open Work Permit can be applied for simultaneously, however the dependent spouse must provide evidence that the principal worker is presently employed at the time of application and will remain employed in a NOC 0, A or B occupation. Further information can be found in the Help Centre: Can my spouse or common-law partner work in Canada?

threads.answer:

Question: I would like to inquire about a situation regarding needing to amend an immigration document (Work Permit). If the location of employment is mistakenly (wrong city within the same province) input by the immigration officer on a valid work permit, is the foreign worker authorized to work in the city (correct location) while waiting for the amendments to be completed? All other information (Employer, occupation, etc.) are correct.
Response: If the work location was noted on the work permit incorrectly, but the foreign national is working at the location that is consistent with what was indicated on the Offer of Employment or LMIA submitted to IRCC before the work permit was issued, then the employer should not be found in non-compliance with any IRPR condition regarding employment of a foreign national. It is recommended that the employer maintain any documents supporting the fact that the foreign national is and has been only working in the location stated on the Offer since the issuance of the work permit.

Could you kindly advise me of what kind of proof is pretty solid when the client needs to prove that he/she will leave Canada when his/her work permit expires?
RESPONSE:
There are no specific documents that prove that they will leave Canada when the work permit expires. The requirement under R200(1)(b) is that the officer must be satisfied’ that the person will leave Canada. In general, officers must assess applicants' intentions based on criteria such as
the length of time that the client will be spending in Canada means of support obligations and ties to the home country the purpose and the context of the stay the credibility of documents and information submitted past compliance with requirements of the IRPA and the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR) that are applicable to temporary residents (visitors, students and workers), as well as information available in biographic and biometric information sharing
For example, the officer will evaluate if the person will try to extend their work permit once it expires; if they have enough financial ability and family support to return home or if the individual has any acquaintances or connections in Canada that are stronger than those outside of Canada. It is the foreign national's responsibility to satisfy the officers with their answers. For more information you can review the publically available instructions for officers at: Temporary residents: Eligibility and admissibility considerations

Vous trouverez ci-dessous la réponse approuvée à votre question.
Un étudiant qui a déposé une demande de permis de travail coop n’a pas le droit de commencer son stage tant que le traitement de sa demande et le permis de travail lui soit émis.
Toutefois, selon les conditions de son permis d'étude, un étudiant peut avoir le droit de travailler.
En effet, les étudiants qui fréquentent un établissement d’enseignement postsecondaire à plein temps peuvent
travailler sans permis de travail sur le campus de l’université ou du collège qu’ils fréquentent à plein temps [R186f)]. Cette autorisation sera indiquée sur leur permis d’études et sera valable pour la durée de validité du permis d’études lié
à l’établissement où ils sont inscrits à plein temps.
En espérant que ces informations vous seront utiles,
Merci! ********* **********

Bonjour,
Veuillez trouver ci-dessous les réponses à vos questions.
1- Est-ce que par l'expression « la portion d’études offerte au Canada » on souhaite indiquer qu'une fréquentation scolaire en présentiel dans l'établissement a lieu ? Réponse : Pas tout à fait. Si le programme offre une partie du programme qui requiert la présence de l’étudiant au Canada, cela est considéré comme « la portion d’études offerte au Canada ». Certains cours à distance comprennent une partie du programme au Canada (p. ex. des séances spéciales de tutorat ou d'examen final) qui exige la présence physique de l’étudiant dans le pays. Ainsi, si la totalité du programme d'études a une durée de plus de six mois, l'étudiant doit obtenir un permis d'études pour la partie du programme offerte au Canada, même si la durée de la partie au Canada est de moins de six mois.
2- L'étudiant étranger suivant intégralement ses cours à distance sans fréquentation scolaire tout en étant au Canada est-il requis de posséder un permis d’études? Réponse : Ceci ne s'applique que pour l’apprentissage à distance. L'apprentissage à distance est offert sous diverses formes : en ligne, par correspondance ou par Internet. L'apprentissage à distance est un processus dans le cadre duquel la technologie est utilisée de manière à ce que l'étudiant n'ait pas besoin d'être physiquement présent à l'endroit où se donne l'enseignement. Puisque, par définition, l'apprentissage à distance ne requiert pas que l'étudiant se trouve au Canada, aucun permis d'études ne doit être délivré pour ce type de cours. Par exemple, si l'étranger ne peut entreprendre des études en raison d'une condition lui ayant été imposée relativement à son permis de travail, il peut suivre des cours à distance. Pour plus d’informations, veuillez-vous référer à notre site internet.
Nous espérons que ces informations vous seront utiles.
La boîte aux lettres des représentants de l'immigration

threads.question:
From Dear Madam/Sir;
If a student transfers from one full time program at a DLI to another without completing the 1st program, can they work before the new program starts?

Thank you for your time.
threads.answer:
Hello,
Thank you for contacting the Immigration Representatives mailbox. We hope the following answers your question.
International students can work off campus without a work permit if they meet all of these requirements: they're a full-time student at a designated learning institution (DLI)
- they're enrolled in a post-secondary academic, vocational or professional training program or a secondary-level vocational training program (Quebec only)
- their study program
is at least 6 months long and leads to a degree, diploma or certificate they've started studying they have a Social Insurance Number (SIN)
They can only start working in Canada when their study program has started. They can't work before they start their studies.
More information can be found here.
Regards,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.subject: PGWP processing delay and work authorization
threads.question:
Hi there,
and Cizenship Canedaot Citoyenneté Canada
As the processing delays on certain applications continue to be impacted by the ongoing Ukrainian situation, most of our students who applied for a PGWP in Canada are still waiting for their applications to be processed. Recently our office is getting many inquiries on work authorization beyond the date stated on the IRCC's acknowledgement of receipt after PGWP submission in January, 2022. We are seeing a lot of students have a letter from IRCC indicating a specific date that they are allowed to work until and a lot of them are approached by their current employer for another official confirmation from IRCC to extend their interim work authorization as their PGWP applications are still under process.
We'd like to confirm that as per R186 (W), students who met the PGWP eligibility and submitted a PGWP application before their study permit expires are, by law, allowed to continue working after the date stated on their IRCC acknowledgement of receipt is passed. Below is part of the letter that's creating confusion now: "Please attach this letter to your present Study permit Number as proof that you are authorized to work for any employer, in any occupation with no restriction on hours until May 27, 2022 or a decision is made on your application, whichever is first”
We understand these receipts from IRCC were created in response to the prolonged processing time and had an intention to remove barriers for finding employment for PGWP applicants. However, as the processing time continue to increase, more and more students started to contact our office for support on getting another official confirmation from IRCC to extend their work authorization as employers interpreted the letter as PGWP applicants can only work until the date indicated on the IRCC receipt of PGWP application.
Keep well and be kind,
Citoenneté Canada
threads.answer:
Hello,
Thank you for contacting the Immigration Representatives mailbox. We hope the following answers your question. ***
Students who met the PGWP eligibility and submitted a PGWP application before their study permit expires are, by law, allowed to continue working after the date stated on their IRCC acknowledgement of receipt is passed. Officers should understand that the validity date of the letter (IMM 0127 E – WP-EXT for PGWP) in no way overrides the authority of paragraph R186(w), which allows foreign nationals who meet the requirements to continue working until a final decision is made on their work permit application.
The letter has a 120-day validity from the date of receipt, which corresponds with IRCC's service standard for in-Canada applications. In cases where the 120 days have passed and no decision has been rendered, the eligible applicants are still authorized to work, and may request continued proof of authorization to work using the IRCC web form.
Students can also show their employer proof that they submitted their PGWP application. Valid forms of proof include
a copy of their work permit application
proof that they paid their fees a copy of postal or courier tracking information.
You may find more information on our website.
We hope that this information is helpful to you.
Thank you.
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

QUESTION: I am following up regarding this 2020 ImmRep response and requesting that its accuracy be looked at further as it appears to contravene the Guidelines and the intention behind c20, and appears to conflate ICT and C20. The ImmRep response appears to say that a foreign worker must first be employed by an organization outside of Canada before they can be transferred to Canada under C20.
However, the online Guidelines for C20, say nothing about the foreign worker first having to be employed outside of Canada, only that the Canadian employer demonstrate that Canadians have similar reciprocal opportunities aboard and that entry should result in a neutral labour market impact.
If IRCC requires that FWs first be employed outside of Canada in order to benefit, is there a minimum amount of time they must be employed outside of Canada?
2020 ImmRep response: Question: In order to be eligible to use the C-20 category, does the TFW have to already be employed within the multinational group, outside of Canada, at the time of the work permit application?
Response: Note that there is no experience requirement for C20, however, being currently employed with the company is a key feature for companies to be allowed to use C20. Commencing employment with the company upon arrival in Canada would not provide the foreign national or Canadian employee the opportunity of being able to benefit from an exchange of knowledge or experience.
If the employee is not already working for the organization abroad, it would be difficult to determine how they could take part in the organization's global exchange program. In order for reciprocity to exist, an employer/employee relationship must be created in advance of the consideration for the LMiA exemption.
RESPONSE: The initial response from 2020 is correct. The administrative code C20, is the code used for paragraph 205(b) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations which states : R205(b) A work permit may be issued under section 200 to a foreign national who intends to perform work that would create or maintain reciprocal employment of Canadian citizens or permanent residents of Canada in other countries;
It is the requirement for reciprocal employment' that ensures that the foreign national is employed in the foreign company before they are rotated to Canada. Reciprocity normally requires exchange agreements as it can apply between different companies with no qualifying relationship or it can be part of the global HR plan
migration, Réfugiés Information disclosed under the Access to Information Ac
for one multinational company. There is also no specific occupation or knowledge requirements. If the foreign worker is not employed with the foreign company before they are relocated to Canada, then there is no reciprocal employment’ opportunity. It would essentially just be the Canadian company hiring a foreign worker off the street' which is not reciprocal. Unlike intra-company transferees, there is no specific term of employment needed with the foreign company.
Intra-company transferees are assessed with the administrative code C12 under paragraph R205(a) that the foreign nationals work would create or maintain significant social, cultural or economic benefits or opportunities for Canadian citizens or permanent residents. It requires a specific occupation or specialized knowledge and that their be a qualifying relationship between the foreign and Canadian entity.
The prograi delivery instructions for officers : Reciprocal employment general guidelines R205(b). C20 "say nothing about the foreign worker first having to be employed outside of Canada" because they are written for processing officers who understand that reciprocal employment means that the foreign national is rotating from a position they already hold outside of Canada for a foreign company into a position inside Canada.

A foreign national's temporary resident status ends upon their departure from Canada.
