Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox. We appreciate your patience.
Please note that this service is to give general functional guidance, thus we are not able to provide case specific advice.
Inquiry: Can you please clarify if a TFW in the following situation would receive points for arranged employment based on the Federal Skilled Worker Selection Factor Grid:
Question 1: TFW has an employer-specific work permit based on Free Trade Agreement as a professional and is working full-time in Canada for the employer named on the work permit but has not worked for employer for an entire year yet
Answer 1: The work experience minimum requirement for FSW program, applicants must be at least one year of continuous work full time, or equivalent part-time, paid work experience acquired in the last ten years and must also demonstrate the performance of duties set out in the occupational description(s) in the applicants primary NOC. This includes all the essential duties and most of the main duties listed. If they are selected under the Federal Skilled Worker (FSW) class, they need to continue working for the employer who offered them arranged employment through to visa issuance or the points for FSW (out of 67) will be removed.
Question 2: The employer obtains approval from ESDC to support the TFWs PR application (they have an approved Express Entry LMIA that was fee-exempt; therefore, TFW cannot apply for WP, but doesn't need to because they already have a WP through the IMP)
Answer 2: A work permit on its own is not a job offer, even if it is an open work permit. Applicants must have a valid job offer from a Canadian employer. The job offer must be in writing, and must set out details of the job the employer is offering such as the pay and deductions, job duties, conditions of employment (hours of work).
Question 3: The employer makes the TFW an offer of employment that meets all the requirements of IRPR 82 (1).
Answer 3: There are few different ways for applicants to obtain points for arranged employment. As per subsection 82(2) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations, up to 10 points will be awarded to an applicant for arranged employment if they are able to perform and are likely to accept and carry out the employment, and meet the requirements for a valid offer of employment. Please note that no points is awarded for arranged employment if the employer making the offer is an embassy, high commission or consulate in Canada or an employer who is referred to in any of subparagraph
Please note that in order to gain points for arranged employment; the applicant must meet the definition as described under section 29 of the Ministerial Instructions respecting the Express Entry system on the date they receive their invitation to apply and on the date they applied for permanent residence. If invited to apply, applicants must be prepared to substantiate all work experience claimed in their profile and provide evidence that their claimed experience corresponds to the occupational descriptions(s) as set out in the NOC codes they have specified on their applications.
Please be advised that the assessment of an application is based on a case-by-case basis; each application will be considered on its own merits, with a final decision based on a review of all the information available to the officer at the time of decision. The onus is always on the applicant to provide sufficient documentation to satisfy an officer that they meet the requirements.
We trust that this information will assist you.
Sincerely,
Immigration Representatives Mailbox

No, it is not possible for a person to restore their status to a different one from what they previously held. An applicant can only restore their status to that of a temporary resident and to the authorization that they held immediately prior to the restoration application. As an example, a student who lost their status cannot apply to restore temporary resident status with authorization to work. However, if the applicant is eligible to restore the status/authorization they previously held, they may submit an application for a different type of authorization at the same time. For example, a temporary resident who held a study permit and has lost their status can apply in Canada for restoration of their temporary resident status and study permit. They may also apply and pay for a work permit if they meet the requirements of the work permit program they are applying for. If they are approved for the study permit, the work permit application will then be processed. The fees for the study or work permit must be paid in addition to the restoration fee, unless they are otherwise exempt.

### IPG Student Unit Admin / Admin Unité des étudiants OPI (IRCC)
Good day,
Please see below the approved response;
Regarding the first question; The visitor visa for the son cannot be applied for from inside Canada, he must leave and apply from outside Canada.
Approved response: That is correct. If a client wishes to apply for a new TRV they must apply outside of Canada. Only foreign nationals who hold a valid work or study permit and who are in Canada are eligible to apply for a TRV from within Canada and only under certain conditions.
Regarding the other questions;
Minor children already in Canada are authorized to study without a study permit at the pre-school, primary or secondary level if
- they are either accompanying parents claiming refugee status or are claimants themselves; one of their parents (biological or adoptive) is a Canadian citizen or permanent resident; one of their parents (biological or adoptive) is authorized to work or study in Canada; this includes temporary residents who are work permit holders, study permit holders, visitor status holders (e.g., visitor record holders) who are either authorized to work without a
permit, as per section 186 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR), or
authorized to study without a permit, as per section R188; or
- neither parent is physically in Canada.
Minor children intending to study are required to apply for a study permit before entering Canada.
It should be noted that minor children of a temporary resident (visitor) who is not authorized to work or study require a study permit to study in Canada.

, (IRCC), and the Canadian Border Services Agency (CBSA) share responsibility for the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA). While IRCC has responsibility for overall immigration policy, issuing visas, the CBSA is responsible for enforcing the Act. CBSA's enforcement role includes determining the length of time a temporary resident may remain in Canada, per subsection 183(2) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR). The standard length of stay for visitors in Canada is 6 months, but this is authorized and established at the discretion of the border service officer (BSO) at the port of entry (POE). The BSO has the sole authority to authorize a foreign national to enter Canada and may issue a visitor record to a temporary resident at the POE on their arrival to Canada. A foreign national may apply to extend their temporary resident status beyond the initial period granted for their stay by a BSO at the POE or by a previous in-Canada extension. In the scenario that you have described, the spouse may be eligible to apply for a visitor record from within Canada. They must apply for a visitor record before their current status expires.

threads.answer:
June 13, 2022 12:38 PM
IPG ADMIN Worker Unit / Unité des travailleurs ADMIN OPI (IRCC) RE: NOC Code Question -- REP-2022-1044 -- Due 2022-06-13
Good day,
Thank you for reaching out the IPG mailbox. Please see the answer to your question below.
QUESTION: A question about NOC code 6221 (Technical Sales Associates) and NOC code 6421 (Retail Sales Persons).
(a renowned telecommunication company), as a Sales One of my clients is employed with Associate performing same job duties prescribed in NOC 6221. Also note that, Telecommunication sales representatives are in examples of this NOC code.
I am completely aware of the fact that job duties matter the most, however to be 110% sure, I am asking that sales associates in telecommunication companies come under NOC 6221 or NOC 6421?
RESPONSE:
Please note the IPG-TRPD does not does not provide guidance on which NOC code to use. The National Occupational Classification (NOC) is Canada's national system for describing occupations is led by ESDC and Statistics Canada, and is available publicly where clients can where an occupation is classified or to learn about its main duties, educational requirements or other useful information (please visit: [https://noc.esdc.gc.ca](https://noc.esdc.gc.ca)).
In terms of addressing the questions in general sense, according to the National Occupational Classification (2016, Version 1.3), NOC code 6221 (Technical Sales Specialists – Wholesale Trade) specifically excludes NOC code 6421 (Retail Salespersons). Though there is some overlap across both NOC codes, a major distinction lies in that Retail Salespersons sell primarily to consumers, whereas Technical Sales Specialists – Wholesale Trade sell primarily to “governments and to
commercial and industrial establishments in domestic and international localities."
There are other important distinctions to also note regarding the main job duties and employment requirements. Technical Sales Specialists – Wholesale Trade positions usually require a university degree or college diploma in a program related to the product or service. These positions also skew much higher on the median and high end of the prevailing hourly wage spectrum. This information may be used by officers in their assessments of Work Permit applications. For more information on the prevailing wages on both positions, please see Canada's (ESDC) Job Bank statistics below. Technical Sales Specialist in Canada Retail Salesperson in Canada
With this in mind, I invite you to compare the two NOC codes on the ESDC website and select the one which is most
appropriate for your client. I have linked them below for your convenience.
NOC 6221 - Technical Sales Specialists-Wholesale Trade NOC 6421 - Retail Salespersons
*As an aside, please note that it is possible these NOC code descriptions/details could change with the upcoming implementation of NOC 2021 this fall (TBD)
In closing, apologies, but we are not in the position to provide a recommendation on which NOC code to assign to the application in discussion, yet we hope the information above is of use for the assessment.

If a child, born outside Canada, to a Canadian parent enters Canada as a visitor, are they obligated to extend their status as a visitor while they wait for their proof of citizenship file to be processed? Thank you

IPG Visitors Unit Admin / Admin Unite des Visiteurs OPI (IRCC); Maloley-Valley.Danny;

Good morning Immigration Reps,
The parent is obligated to maintain status as a visitor for the child in order to maintain legal status in Canada. If the current temporary resident status is still valid the parent can apply for an extension. For any permit, applications should always be submitted at least 30 days before the current status expires. The original temporary status as a visitor continues under the same conditions until the application is finalized and you have been notified of the decision.

If the student leaves Canada, then when can the student return? The next term is September 2022. If the student returns, can the student return as a student, if the student is holding a valid study permit? Or must she return as a visitor?
Thanks. Regards,
On Mon, May 16, 2022 at 7:35 AM wrote:
Good day,
Please see below the approved response.
Students may be required or may wish to take leave from their studies while in Canada. For the purpose of assessing if a student is actively pursuing their studies, any leave taken from a program of studies in Canada should not exceed 150 days from the date the leave commenced and must be authorized by their DLI.
A student on leave who begins or resumes their studies within 150 days from the date the leave commenced (that is, the date the leave was granted by the institution) is considered to be actively pursuing studies during their leave. If a student does not resume their studies within 150 days, they should do either of the following:
- change their status (that is, change to visitor status or worker status)
- leave Canada
Lnomdn

Please note that the student cannot work on or off campus during an authorized leave from their study program, even if their study permit says they are allowed to work in Canada.
We hope that this information is helpful to you.

threads.question:
Madame, Monsieur,
Je sollicite votre assistance afin de m'éclairer face à la situation suivante.
Nous avons un client, un étudiant étranger mineur, qui étudie actuellement au Canada avec une
fiche de visiteur l'autorisant à fréquenter l'école secondaire, et ce, considérant qu'un de ses parents
détient un permis de travail valide.
Celui-ci souhaite travailler pendant les vacances d'été. Afin qu'il puisse occuper un emploi durant la
saison estivale, nous avons déterminé qu'un permis d'études pourrait être une avenue envisageable.
À cet effet, nous avons déposé une demande de Certificat d’acceptation du Québec (CAQ) pour
études auprès du MIFI. Toutefois, nous avons reçu une correspondance du MIFI indiquant que notre
client est exempté d'obtenir un CAQ, puisquil étudie actuellement avec une fiche de visiteur, en vertu de l'article 20 (5) du Règlement sur l'immigration au Québec
Considérant ce qui précède, pouvons-nous tout de même produire sa demande de permis d'études
sans détenir un CAQ valide? Si ce n'est pas le cas, pouvez-vous nous indiquer les démarches à
suivre afin que notre client puisse travailler cet été.
Merci à l'avance,
Citoenneté Canada

d'études -- REP-2022-1004 -- Due 2022-06-06
Bonjour,
Vous trouverez ci-dessous la réponse approuvée à votre question.
Il est établi que les enfants mineurs se trouvant déjà au Canada sont autorisés à étudier sans permis d’études aux niveaux préscolaire, primaire et secondaire dans le cas où l'un de leurs parents (biologique ou adoptif) est autorisé à travailler ou à étudier au Canada, ce qui inclut les résidents temporaires qui : sont titulaires d’un permis de travail,
Il convient donc de noter que dans la question posée plus bas, l’étranger mineur n’a pas besoin d’un permis d’étude pour étudier au niveau secondaire, considérant qu’un de ses parents détient un permis de travail valide. Étant donné qu’il est exempté d’un permis d’étude et d’un CAQ, il serait plus envisageable pour l’étudiant étranger de faire une demande pour la modification des conditions sur sa fiche de visiteur afin que celui-ci puisse travailler pendant la période estivale d'été.
Cette demande de modification des conditions sur la fiche de visiteur peut se faire en ligne ou possiblement à un point d’entrée (à la discrétion de l'agent). Vous pouvez consulter les liens suivants pour de plus amples informations;
1.[http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/temp/visa/processing-traitement/record-fiche-](http://cicintranet.ci.gc.ca/connexion/tools-outils/temp/visa/processing-traitement/record-fiche-) fra.aspx#Work permit and
Dispenses de permis de travail Voir la liste des étrangers pouvant être autorisés à travailler sans permis.
Les étrangers admissibles à la dispense de permis de travail de 120 jours ou à la dispense de permis de travail de courte durée (de 15 à 30 jours) peuvent demander une fiche du visiteur au point d’entrée.
Si l’étranger en fait la demande et que toutes les autres exigences sont respectées, l'ASF lui délivrera une fiche du visiteur. La fiche du visiteur permettra de valider le statut du résident
temporaire comme étant dispensé du permis de travail et d’appuyer sa demande de numéro
d’assurance sociale présentée à Service Canada.
La fiche du visiteur délivrée comportera des remarques précisant la capacité de l’étranger de travailler sans permis. Les remarques suivantes peuvent figurer sur la fiche du visiteur :
- « Dispensé du permis de travail à titre de [titre du poste] »; « Dispensé du permis de travail aux termes de l’article R186 », un alinéa peut être mentionné, par exemple l’alinéa R186s);
- « Dispense du permis de travail de courte durée (de 120 jours) – Politique d’intérêt public »;
and Cizenship Canadaot Citoyenneté Canada
- « Dispense du permis de travail de courte durée (de 15 ou 30 jours) – Politique d’intérêt public ».
Voir la section Fiches du visiteur dans les instructions sur les dispenses de permis de travail de courte durée (de 120 jours) pour en savoir plus.

Question: We are seeking clarification on qualifying work experience for the Federal Skilled Worker Class. We understand that full-time work experience must be accumulated over a continuous 12 month period, but is it a requirement that part-time work experience be accumulated over a continuous period of 24 months for it to be valid? Does part-time allow breaks in employment? We have not found clear confirmation on this subject and would
Answer: As per section 75(2)(a) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations, a foreign national is considered
"within the 10 years before the date on which their application for a permanent resident visa is made, they have accumulated, over a continuous period, at least one year of full-time work experience, or the equivalent in part-time work, in the occupation identified by the foreing national in their application as their primary occupation, other than a restricted occupation, that is listed in Skill Type 0 Management Occupations or Skill Level A or B of
In short, the applicant must have a minimum of 1,560 hours of qualifying work experience, which was obtained over a continuous period. The example used on our website shows that an applicant can meet this requirement by working 15 hours/week for 24 months, which would equal 1,560 hours. The applicant can work as many part-time jobs as needed to meet the requirement (more or less than 15 hours/week) so long as it adds up to 1,560 hours. We do not count any
Please be advised that the assessment of an application is based on a case-by-case basis, considering the particular circumstances in conjunction with the supporting documentation available to the officer. The onus is always on the applicant to provide sufficient documentation to satisfy an officer that they meet the requirements.
